name: scale_hv_angle
hypothesis: Doubling sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity via input scaling, and increasing side‑thruster logits, should improve wind compensation without harming nominal performance.

name: aggressive_scale_hv_angle
hypothesis: Increase sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, amplify side‑thruster logits, and boost hidden layer 2 to improve wind compensation under strong crosswind while preserving nominal performance.

name: enhanced_side_thrusters
hypothesis: Amplify sensitivity to horizontal position, velocity, angle, and angular velocity, and boost side‑engine logits via output scaling and bias, to better counter strong crosswind while preserving nominal performance.

name: targeted_input_output_scale
hypothesis: Increase sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, and amplify side‑engine logits while adding a small negative offset to side‑engine bias to avoid spurious firing in calm conditions. This should improve crosswind compensation without hurting nominal performance.

name: wind_compensation_v2
hypothesis: Amplify sensitivity to horizontal position, velocity, angle, and angular velocity, and boost side‑thruster logits (with a small positive bias) while slightly increasing hidden layer 2 magnitude, to better counter strong crosswind and improve landing on the pad.

name: moderate_input_scale_hidden1_output_offset
hypothesis: Increase sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, slightly amplify the first hidden layer, and boost side‑engine logits while applying a small negative bias to side‑engine actions. This should improve wind compensation without causing excess side‑thruster firing in calm conditions, preserving nominal performance.

name: strong_input_side_scale_hidden
hypothesis: Scale horizontal position, horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity more aggressively, boost side‑engine logits with a small positive bias, and slightly amplify both hidden layers. This should give the controller stronger corrective actions against the strong crosswind while staying stable in nominal conditions.

name: aggressive_input_side_scale
hypothesis: Increase sensitivity to horizontal position, horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, strongly boost side‑engine logits with a larger scale and a negative offset to avoid spurious firing, and slightly amplify the first hidden layer. This should give the controller stronger lateral correction under strong crosswind while keeping nominal performance safe.

name: enhanced_input_output_side
hypothesis: Scale horizontal position, horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity strongly, amplify both hidden layers modestly, and increase side‑engine logits (with a small positive bias) to give the controller more aggressive lateral correction under strong crosswind while keeping nominal performance stable.

name: balanced_input_hidden_output
hypothesis: Increase sensitivity to horizontal position, horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, modestly amplify both hidden layers, and boost side‑thruster and main‑engine logits (with a small negative bias for side thrusters and a small positive bias for the main engine) to improve lateral and vertical control under strong crosswind while preserving nominal performance.

name: full_input_output_scale_modest_hidden
hypothesis: Scale horizontal position, horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity strongly, modestly amplify both hidden layers, and boost side‑thruster logits heavily while also increasing main‑engine strength and adding a small negative bias to side thrusters and a small positive bias to the main engine. This should give the controller stronger lateral correction and better vertical control under strong crosswind without degrading nominal performance.

name: balanced_aggressive_input_output
hypothesis: Strongly increase sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity, modestly amplify both hidden layers, and heavily boost side‑thruster logits while also giving the main engine a moderate boost and small bias adjustments. This should provide stronger lateral correction and better vertical control under strong crosswind without causing instability.
